title: Chief Expert- Overall ITC (International) – BID Position
description:
SYSTRA is one of the world's leading engineering and consulting groups specializing in public transport and mobility solutions. For over 65 years, the Group has been committed to helping cities and regions develop by creating, improving and modernizing their transport infrastructure and systems.
   

  

 Context
   

  

 In India, SYSTRA is an international consulting and engineering company operating in the fields of Metros, High Speed Rail, Railways, Roads, Buildings, Urban planning, and Water \& Environment for public and private organizations.
   

  

 Our engineers work with passion to deliver the most reliable, cost\-effective and made\-to measures solutions allowing end users to move seamlessly.
   

  

 SYSTRA’s unique expertise is backed with a reputation built through technical excellence delivered on projects. Thanks to our know\-how of our employees spread across India, we are present at all stages from upstream studies to operation and maintenance. We provide a comprehensive solution to manage all kinds of missions: Detailed Design Consultant, Project Management, Independent checking services.
   

  

 SYSTRA India’s comprehensive know\-how and expertise in Railways provides a wide spectrum of solutions for any challenge (Building a new rail link, doubling the capacity, gauge conversion, upgrading a network, improving the performance of existing lines, etc.).
   

  

 Our extensive experience encompasses, Bridges, station buildings, Depots, Earthwork \& Track Works, Power Supply and Transmission, Signaling \& Telecommunications, Rolling Stock, Utilities diversion and yard re\-modelling etc.
   

  

 Our services cover the entire life cycle of the project implementation.
   

  

 Currently, we are bidding for High Speed Rail projects across India. The position of
   

  

 Chief Expert\- Overall ITC is the key position in these BIDs.
   

  

 Missions/Main Duties
   

  

* To act as lead member in ITC Coordination team.
* Prepare and issue ITC Overall Basic Document base don the ITC Overall Basic Document (Preliminary).
* Prepare integrated Overall ITC Detail Plan based on the ITC Overall Basic Document and Overall ITC Plans issued by each Contractor.
* Coordinate between Contractors/Parties related to the Overall ITC, concerning matters such as scheduling and location for installing and attaching measuring devices on the Rolling Stock at the Depot.
* Witness the tests related to Overall ITC (as applicable).
* Evaluate test results along with respective package Engineer and advise corrective actions and/or additional tests to the Contractors.
* Examine and determine countermeasures along with respective package Engineer against issues related to two or more packages.
* Issue summarized/ compiled progress reports and recommendation on the Overall ITC, at the appropriate time.
* Submitting all necessary documents and have discussions etc. with CMRS / RDSO/ other Statutory Authorities to obtain approvals.


 Profile/Skills
   

  

- Nationality: Expat Only

- Age:

* Less than 60 Years (preferred)
* Must be below 70 years


- Educational Qualification:

* Postgraduate / Doctorate in relevant field (preferred)
* Graduate Engineering degree in relevant field (minimum)


- Experience:

* Overall more than 25 years of experience in Railways/Metro.
* More than 15 years of experience in Overall Integration, Testing and Commissioning (ITC) of various systems including Operation \& Maintenance (O\&M) in \*High\-Speed / Semi High\-Speed / Metro Rail Projects.
* More than 5 years of experience as in\-charge of Integration, Testing and Commissioning (ITC) in \*High\-Speed Rail Project(s).
* High Speed: ETCS based projects with operational speed equal or greater than 250 Kmph
* Semi High Speed: Projects with operational speed equal to or greater than 160 Kmph
* Metro: Excluding LRT/Tram/Monorail Systems


 We commit to put people who join us at the heart of improving transportation and urban infrastructure efficiency. As we are growing, this is time to be a part of this challenging adventure. It’s not a job \- it’s a career!

It supports the maintenance of efficient and effective workflows, procedures, policies, and inspection programs within the QA documentation cell framework. title: Historian & IT-OT Functional Manager (Manufacturing Function – IT)
description:
We are looking for a Historian \& IT\-OT Functional Manager who will serve as the
 **voice of manufacturing within the IT organization** 
 . The role is the bridge between plant operations and technology.
 



  





**Job Description:** 




**Role: Historian \& IT\-OT Functional Manager (Manufacturing Function – IT)** 




**Designation: Manager** 




**Experience:** 
 12–18 years total, with at least 6 years in pharmaceutical manufacturing operations or manufacturing IT/OT, and at least 4 years in a functional lead or manager role
 



**Education:** 
 B. Pharm, M. Pharm/ B. E, M.E / B. Tech, M.Tech \- Chemical, Instrumentation, Mechanical, Electrical Engineering, Information Technology, or related disciplines.
 



**Location** 
 : Ahmedabad (The position follows plant operating schedules and a 6\-day working week.)
 



  





**Role Summary:** 
 The ideal candidate has
 **worked in or closely with pharma manufacturing** 
 , understands unit operations, batch lifecycle, equipment, and shop\-floor workflows, and also understands how historians, automation, MES, LIMS, and ERP integrate. The individual will own the functional side of historian and IT\-OT solutions from requirement to go\-live and beyond, working with architects, developers, system integrators, and site teams. Also, will understand how the plant runs, translate manufacturing and quality needs into clear IT and OT requirements, and lead implementation through to adoption and measurable business value.
 



  





**Key Responsibilities:** 




**1\. Manufacturing Business Partnering** 



* Act as the primary IT point of contact for Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Maintenance, Warehouse, and Supply Chain teams at plant and corporate levels.
* Understand plant priorities such as throughput, yield, right\-first\-time, batch cycle time, deviation reduction, compliance, and cost, and align IT\-OT initiatives to them.
* Spend regular time on the shop floor to observe processes, identify pain points, and uncover digital opportunities.
* Build trusted relationships with plant heads, production managers, QA heads, and engineering leads.
* Maintain a prioritized demand backlog and business\-aligned roadmap for historian and IT\-OT solutions.



**2\. Business\-to\-IT Requirement Translation** 



* Lead requirement workshops with manufacturing and quality stakeholders to capture business needs, current\-state (as\-is) processes, and desired future state (to\-be).
* Map manufacturing processes end to end, for example process order release, material dispensing, batch execution, in\-process checks, equipment cleaning and status, batch record review, and batch release.
* Translate business needs into structured deliverables:
 **business requirements, User Requirement Specifications (URS), functional specifications (FS), use cases, user stories, process flows, data mapping, and acceptance criteria** 
 .
* Conduct fit\-gap analysis against standard product capabilities and recommend configuration over customization wherever possible.
* Define which process parameters, alarms, events, and batch context need to be captured, contextualized, and reported, and why they matter to the business.
* Clearly explain technical constraints, options, and trade\-offs back to business users in plain language.



**3\. Historian Functional Ownership** 



* Own the functional design of the process historian (e.g., AVEVA PI System, AspenTech IP.21, Honeywell PHD, Proficy) across sites.
* Define with process and engineering teams which tags, critical process parameters (CPPs), critical quality attributes (CQAs), and utilities data must be collected.
* Drive the design of asset hierarchies, templates, batch and event frames, and calculations based on actual equipment and process structure (ISA\-88 / ISA\-95\).
* Specify dashboards, trends, reports, and alerts for production, QA, engineering, and management users.
* Enable business use cases such as:
* Batch trending and golden batch comparison
* Continued Process Verification (CPV) and Annual Product Quality Review (APQR) data support
* Deviation and investigation support with process data
* OEE, downtime, and equipment performance
* Environmental monitoring (HVAC, cleanrooms, differential pressure, temperature, humidity)
* Utilities and energy monitoring (WFI, purified water, steam, compressed air, HVAC)
* Cold chain and storage condition monitoring



**4\. IT\-OT Integration Functional Leadership** 



* Define functional requirements for integration between shop\-floor systems (DCS, PLC, SCADA, BMS, EMS, standalone equipment) and enterprise systems (MES, LIMS, ERP/SAP, QMS, CMMS, WMS).
* Specify business data flows, for example process order download from SAP to MES, material consumption and goods movement back to ERP, equipment status to MES, process data to eBR, and results from LIMS to batch release.
* Work with the IT\-OT Integration Architect and Historian Architect to confirm that technical designs meet business needs.
* Ensure consistent master data and naming across equipment, materials, recipes, and sites.
* Support Pharma 4\.0 initiatives including analytics, AI/ML use cases, digital twins, and predictive maintenance by clearly defining business context and data needs.



**5\. Implementation and Delivery Ownership** 



* Lead the functional workstream of historian and IT\-OT projects from initiation through design, build, testing, deployment, and hypercare.
* Plan functional activities, milestones, resources, and dependencies in coordination with project managers, architects, and system integrators.
* Guide developers and integrators on business logic, configuration, and process understanding.
* Lead
 **User Acceptance Testing (UAT)** 
 : prepare test scenarios with business users, coordinate execution, and track defects to closure.
* Prepare cutover and go\-live plans with site teams, carefully planning around production schedules, campaigns, and shutdowns.
* Provide hypercare support after go\-live and ensure smooth handover to support teams.
* Manage scope changes through a structured change request process.



**6\. GxP Compliance, Validation and Data Integrity** 



* Ensure all solutions meet
 **21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11, GAMP 5, and ALCOA\+** 
 requirements.
* Author or own functional validation documents: URS, FS, functional risk assessments, requirements traceability matrix, UAT/PQ protocols, and validation summary inputs.
* Work closely with QA and CSV teams on validation strategy, including CSA risk\-based approaches.
* Ensure changes follow site change control, impact assessment, and periodic review processes.
* Represent historian and IT\-OT systems during regulatory inspections and audits (USFDA, EMA, MHRA, WHO\-GMP, and local authorities), explaining business use and data flows.



**7\. Change Management, Training and Adoption** 



* Drive user adoption through training programs, SOP updates, work instructions, and user guides.
* Identify and develop super\-users and site champions.
* Collect user feedback after go\-live and drive continuous improvements.
* Track and report business benefits and value realization, such as reduced investigation time, improved OEE, and reduced manual data collection.



**8\. Operations and Continuous Improvement** 



* Act as the functional escalation point for historian and IT\-OT application issues.
* Work with support teams on incident, problem, and change management, and help define business\-aligned SLAs.
* Periodically review system usage and data quality with site teams.
* Standardize solutions and templates across sites to support faster, consistent rollouts.



**9\. Team and Vendor Leadership** 



* Lead and mentor functional analysts and business analysts within the manufacturing IT team.
* Manage system integrators and vendors on functional scope, quality, and timelines.
* Coordinate with global and site IT, OT, automation, cybersecurity, and quality teams.



  





**Required Manufacturing Knowledge** 




 The candidate must have solid, practical understanding of:
 


* **Pharma manufacturing types:** 
 API (chemical synthesis), oral solid dosage (OSD), sterile/injectables, and/or biologics.
* **Unit operations and equipment** 
 , for example dispensing, granulation (RMG, FBD), blending, compression, coating, capsule filling, packaging, reactors, centrifuges, dryers, distillation, filtration, fermentation, chromatography, lyophilization, and aseptic filling, depending on site type.
* **Batch lifecycle:** 
 process order, recipe, BMR/BPR and eBR, in\-process controls, equipment cleaning and status logs, yield reconciliation, batch record review, and batch release.
* **Plant utilities and environment:** 
 HVAC, cleanroom classification, WFI/PW systems, clean steam, compressed air, and environmental monitoring.
* **Quality processes:** 
 deviations, CAPA, change control, OOS/OOT, APQR, and CPV.
* **Maintenance and engineering processes:** 
 calibration, preventive maintenance, equipment qualification, and breakdown management.
* **Manufacturing KPIs:** 
 OEE, yield, cycle time, right\-first\-time, downtime, and batch throughput.



  





**Required Technical and Functional Skills** 



* Strong functional knowledge of process historians, preferably
 **AVEVA PI System** 
 (PI AF, Event Frames, PI Vision).
* Working understanding of automation systems (DCS, PLC, SCADA) such as Emerson DeltaV, Siemens PCS 7/WinCC, Rockwell, or ABB.
* Functional understanding of
 **MES** 
 (Körber PAS\-X, Emerson Syncade, Siemens Opcenter),
 **LIMS** 
 (LabWare, LabVantage, Empower),
 **SAP** 
 (PP\-PI, QM, PM, MM), and QMS platforms (e.g., TrackWise, Veeva QMS).
* Knowledge of ISA\-95, ISA\-88, and basic integration concepts (OPC UA/DA, interfaces, APIs, data flows).
* Strong business analysis skills: process mapping (BPMN/Visio), requirement elicitation, fit\-gap analysis, user stories, and UAT management.
* Hands\-on experience delivering and validating GxP computerized systems.
* Familiarity with project delivery methodologies (Waterfall, Agile, hybrid) and tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, or HP ALM.
* Basic data skills (Excel, SQL, Power BI or similar) to analyze and validate manufacturing data.



  





**Preferred Qualifications** 



* Bachelor's or Master's degree in
 **Pharmacy, Chemical Engineering, Instrumentation, or Mechanical/Electrical Engineering** 
 ; an MBA or IT qualification is a plus.
* Prior experience working
 **in a plant role** 
 (production, engineering, automation, or QA) before moving into IT is highly valued.
* Certifications such as AVEVA/OSIsoft PI, CBAP/PMI\-PBA, PMP/PRINCE2, ITIL, Six Sigma, or Lean.
* Experience with multi\-site or global rollouts and Pharma 4\.0 or digital manufacturing programs.

title: Deployment Textile Engineer
description:
We’re looking for a hands\-on Deployment Textile Engineer to support the deployment and operation of our OneWeave™ 3D weaving technology at our manufacturing partner in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, near Naroda Road.
   

  

 You’ll be the first line of textile technical support onsite, working alongside factory operators, a project manager, field service technician, and unspun’s remote textile and mechanical engineering teams. You’ll investigate what’s happening in production, run tests, analyze results, solve textile and process problems, and turn what we learn on the factory floor into continuous improvement.
   

  

 You’ll also represent unspun at our partner facility, building trusted relationships and helping teams across both organizations work effectively together.
   

  

 When applying, use the word shark in your cover letter.
   

  

**Why This Role Matters**
 OneWeave™ combines textiles, robotics, sensors, software, and industrial automation to create garments and textile products directly from yarn.
   

  

 As we deploy and ramp this technology in production, we need textile engineering expertise directly on the factory floor. When something involving weaving, yarn, materials, fabric quality, or process performance isn’t behaving as expected, you’ll help determine what’s happening, why it’s happening, and what we should do next.
   

  

 You’ll connect what’s happening onsite in Ahmedabad with the teams developing OneWeave™ in the US, helping us improve both the technology and how we operate it.
   

  

**What You'll Do**
* Support the deployment, testing, ramp\-up, and continuous improvement of OneWeave™ at our partner factory
* Serve as the first line of response for weaving, yarn, material, fabric quality, and textile process issues
* Develop and execute test plans, operate OneWeave™ equipment, and support daily textile testing and production runs
* Perform quality testing inspection, analyzing weaving inputs and outputs using quantitative and qualitative data to identify patterns, problems, and opportunities for improvement
* Investigate textile and process issues, determine likely causes, test potential solutions, and document results
* Assess and prioritize issues based on severity, production impact, available workarounds, and urgency
* Partner with factory operations and US\-based textile, mechanical, and development teams to troubleshoot and resolve issues
* Support yarn and material sourcing, supplier communication, testing, and validation for development and production runs
* Work with material vendors and suppliers on testing requirements, standards, and performance
* Develop and improve machine operation and testing SOPs, troubleshooting guides, training manuals, and supporting documentation
* Identify recurring problems and opportunities to improve equipment, materials, processes, documentation, and training
* Provide clear, concise updates to US\-based teams on factory status, testing, project progress, risks, findings, and next steps
* Capture technical information so engineers who aren't physically onsite can understand factory issues and take action


**Who You Are**
 You’re a textile engineer who likes being close to the actual work. You understand fibers, yarns, woven structures, fabric quality, and manufacturing processes, but you’re also comfortable getting onto the factory floor, operating equipment, running tests, and figuring out why something isn’t working as expected.
   

  

 You’re curious and methodical. You don't simply fix a symptom and move on. You gather information, test assumptions, analyze results, and try to understand the underlying cause.
